issues.legal_issue: The statutory power to eject a lessee by force was not the basis for the eviction dispute when the lease remained in force and no termination under that power had occurred.
material_facts: At the time of the auction and the application to the settlement authority, the lessee’s lease was still running.

The lessee had not been evicted when it applied to the settlement authority, and its application did not claim that eviction had occurred under the statutory power to terminate a lease and eject a former lessee.

The application sought protection against eviction on the grounds that the property should have been allotted to the lessee and that the statutory protection for occupants of transferred property applied.
issues.conclusion: The argument that the eviction was unlawful because the statutory power to eject had not been invoked did not arise on the facts of the application and failed as a ground in the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The statutory power to eject by force applies where a lease is terminated under that power, the person consequently ceases to be entitled to possession, and the person fails to surrender possession on demand. Because no such termination or eviction was in issue in the application, the Court did not decide whether the later eviction was unlawful on some other ground. The Court applied section 19 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954, as it stood before the later amendment; it relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_from_administrative_order and lease_still_running and (no_termination_under_ejection_power or application_not_based_on_ejection_power)

predicates.appeal_from_administrative_order: The proceeding is an appeal from an administrative order concerning an eviction dispute.
predicates.lease_still_running: The occupant’s lease remained in force when the relevant application was made.
predicates.no_termination_under_ejection_power: The authority had not terminated the lease under the statutory power that permits ejection after termination and failure to surrender possession.
predicates.application_not_based_on_ejection_power: The occupant’s application did not rely on an eviction under that statutory power as its basis for resisting eviction.
predicates.ejection_power_issue_not_reached: The court does not decide the legality of the eviction under that power because the issue was not raised by the facts and grounds of the application.

issues.definition: When an appeal from an administrative order concerns an occupant whose lease was still running and the application did not rest on an eviction under the statutory ejection power, the court does not decide the legality of eviction under that power.

issues.legal_issue: An auction declaration and approval of a bid do not transfer property where the sale terms require full payment and a sale certificate before ownership is transferred.
material_facts: Property in the compensation pool was put up for public auction, and bidders were declared, including a highest bidder.
The sale terms made the bid subject to approval and provided that ownership would be transferred and a sale certificate issued after the purchase price was paid in full.
The occupant claimed protection from eviction on the basis that the property had been transferred to the auction purchaser.
The occupant did not establish that the purchase price had been paid in full or that a sale certificate had been issued.
issues.conclusion: There had not yet been a transfer of the property to the auction purchaser, so the occupant could not claim the protection that depended on a transfer.
issues.legal_principle: Section 29 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954, gives a qualifying person in lawful possession protection as a tenant of a transferee when notified property is transferred, including protection against eviction for the prescribed period except on specified grounds. Under section 20, a transfer may be made by sale, subject to the rules. Rule 90(3) provides for notice of sale terms; rule 90(8) requires an initial deposit; rule 90(10) makes a bid subject to approval; rule 90(11) requires payment of the balance after approval; and rule 90(15) provides for a sale certificate when the price has been realised in full. In this sale, the terms also expressly made full payment the condition for transfer of ownership. A highest bid or its approval may create a binding contract, but does not itself transfer the property in these circumstances. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: claim_for_protection_after_property_transfer and auction_sale and (bid_not_approved or purchase_price_not_paid_in_full or sale_certificate_not_issued)

predicates.claim_for_protection_after_property_tran: An occupant claims protection against eviction on the basis that property has been transferred to another person.
predicates.auction_sale: The property was offered for sale by public auction under terms governing completion of the sale.
predicates.bid_not_approved: The competent authority had not approved the successful bid.
predicates.purchase_price_not_paid_in_full: The purchaser had not paid the full purchase price required by the sale terms.
predicates.sale_certificate_not_issued: The authority had not issued the sale certificate required by the sale terms to complete the transfer.
predicates.no_transfer_for_tenant_protection: The property has not been transferred for purposes of the occupant’s claimed protection.

issues.definition: Where an occupant claims protection based on a transfer following an auction but the bid remains unapproved, the full price remains unpaid, or the required sale certificate has not issued, the rule treats the property as not yet transferred for that protection.
